_comment: The pre-registration manifest, checked by tools/verify_freeze.py.
This project's methodological claim is an ORDERING claim: the bar was written
down, and only then was the measurement run. That is what makes a reported
number a result rather than a description of the numbers. An ordering claim is
worthless if it cannot be checked, and 'trust us, we froze it first' is not a
check - so every frozen artifact records its SHA-256 here, and one command
verifies that none of them has moved since.
The hashes below were verified against the files on 2026-09-13 and match the
values already quoted in docs/phase2_results.md, docs/train_operating_points_frozen.md
and CLAUDE.md - which is itself the point: the docs and the manifest agree, so
a reader can check either one.
WHEN A HASH CHANGES. A failure here is not automatically misconduct - a
contract can legitimately be amended. But it must be amended DELIBERATELY:
update the hash in the same commit as the change, say what changed and why in
the artifact's own _amendments or in the doc named below, and never after
seeing a result the change would flatter. Anything that edits a gate to fit a
measurement is the exact failure this file exists to make visible.
A frozen file may only be re-frozen by someone who can say what they knew at
the time. If you cannot, the honest move is to re-run the measurement.
LINE ENDINGS ARE PART OF THE HASH. These are raw SHA-256 digests of the bytes
on disk, matching what validateLesionDetectors.m computes at runtime - so a
file converted from LF to CRLF hashes differently with no character changed.
.gitattributes pins config/*.json to eol=lf for exactly this reason. Without
that pin, `* text=auto` gives every Windows checkout CRLF, and a fresh clone
reports a mismatch on a file nobody touched: a true-looking alarm with no
cause, which is the fastest way to teach people to ignore a real one. If you
ever see every artifact move at once, suspect line endings before misconduct.

artifacts.governs: The Module 2 display gate: precision >= 0.50 AND recall >= 0.10 on the IDRiD segmentation TEST split, micro-averaged, FOV-masked, per-lesion component matching.
artifacts.why_it_must_not_move: Three of four lesion channels FAIL this gate and are hidden from the clinical report because of it. Loosening it would put microaneurysm counts at 0.028 precision in front of a clinician. The file was frozen before validateLesionDetectors ran for the first time, and results/lesion_validation.mat records this hash so the ordering stays checkable after the fact.

artifacts.frozen_by: fitLesionOperatingPoint.m, on the IDRiD TRAIN split only
artifacts.governs: The shipped dark-lesion operating point. Stage 1 alone won on both channels, so applyClassifier = false.
artifacts.why_it_must_not_move: Selected on TRAIN specifically so the held-out TEST split could certify it. Re-selecting on TEST would mean the display gate was certifying a number chosen to pass it.

artifacts.governs: Snapshot of record: the operating points as they stood at the moment the 2x2 patch-geometry x threshSD ablation started.
artifacts.why_it_must_not_move: It is the evidence that the ablation did not change the shipped configuration. It is expected to be byte-identical to config/lesion_operating_points.json - see must_match below - and if the two ever diverge, one of them moved after the ablation.

artifacts.frozen: 2026-09-11, amended to v1.1.0 the same day (B12, logged in _amendments)
artifacts.governs: The referable-DR endpoint: ICDR >= 2 OR referable DME, with per-dataset dme_encoding (IDRiD == 2, Messidor-2 == 1, APTOS none). Also the three reported endpoints and the operating-point freeze policy.
artifacts.why_it_must_not_move: The whole headline claim is stated against this endpoint, and the Messidor-2 read that tested it is SPENT - it cannot be repeated under a different definition. A silent change here would retroactively invalidate the external result. B12 is the cautionary case: a single global DME threshold matched nothing on Messidor-2 and quietly degraded the primary endpoint to DR-only, returning a plausible number with no error.
Measured, not guessed - and the gate's effect on grading was measured too (-9.2pp specificity). Any change invalidates that measurement.

artifacts.governs: Every Module 5 parameter, each tagged SOURCED / DERIVED / ASSUMED.
artifacts.why_it_must_not_move: It is the contract screening_params.m defers to, and the reason the duplicate constants that disagreed were removed. Blocker B11 is precisely what happens when Module 5 numbers come from somewhere else.
artifacts.note: This one is the most likely to change legitimately - several values are ASSUMED and are waiting on real measurements (technician time per patient, clinician review time). Update the hash in the same commit and say what moved.
